variants.direction:
L57. AFT: replace L52's thin raised crossbar with a LOWER, DEEPER, more solid transverse stern crown. Keep approximately its original span and downturned end returns, but give the central body a broad forward-raked face and an unbroken slanted top plane. Integrate the end mounts directly into the stern shoulders, leaving only functional engine/cargo clearances. It must read as a shaped load-bearing rear component, not a car spoiler on two thin posts. The outer ends turn slightly downward/inward like a compact enclosing cornice; no horn tips, no decorative central notch. A quiet shallow fan relief on its central face is contained by a broad uninterrupted upper border, subtly suggesting restrained grandeur.
WINGS: TWO broad, solid overlapping trapezoidal LEAVES on each side. Together they create a nearly continuous clipped-delta/trapezoid outline, between the native fan and the broad Order wing, with a long straight leading edge, clearly clipped outer tips and a stepped trailing contour. Make them substantial aircraft-like plates of varying width, not the old three thin triangular fan fingers minus one. Keep native red radial artwork, but compress the ray composition toward the roots, with calmer outer panels. Fifth reference: use ONLY the native rotary nesting principle and front root location; reduce to two newly designed full leaves per side. In STOWED rotate these two full-size leaves backward to overlap along the outer hull. New mechanism is proposed, not already validated. Keep L52 hull and cockpit unchanged. The gesture is a compact enclosing stern crown and a broad restrained rotating fan. Label L57.
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / constrained redesign from a selected base sheet.
Create ONE new concept sheet for the pirate Liberty elite from Freelancer. The owner has explicitly selected L52 as the base for further CONCEPT exploration. Preserve its main hull, native LI identity and recessed cargo layout. Change primarily the AFT SPOILER / TAIL STRUCTURE and WING SHAPES. Do not continue adding arbitrary collar notches or gaps.

INPUT ROLES:
1. L52, selected design BASE. Preserve its exact multi-faceted lower block, modest raised divergent upper shoulders, intact collar, recessed central cargo deck, relative proportions and native rust-red/ochre/pale artwork. Do not replace the main hull or add new obelisk shapes. Ignore perspective exaggeration of its cockpit; image 2 controls the actual cabin.
2. IMMUTABLE original li_pir_elite cockpit: original low rounded capsule, shell, size, pane boundaries, thin frames and blue-grey glass. Do not replace it with the different or_elite cockpit or stretch/enlarge it.
3. Actual native li_pir_elite: primary material/identity and TWO unequal vertically stacked polygonal engines. Keep that engine arrangement and scale. The original wing fans and transverse spoiler are allowed to change, as specified below.
4. Actual or_elite: only an example of the permissible extent of TAIL and WING redesign within this lineage. Study its broad coherent clipped triangular wing outline, solid root shoulders and rising raked aft crest. Do not copy its different cabin, grey/green palette, third engine, full body or literal design wholesale.
5. Motion reference, whose exact role is specified in the variant.

SHARED CONCEPT: a subtle pirate 'anti-Empire' interpretation of Liberty's ceremonial Art Deco. In the fictional art direction, the owners have appropriated official grandeur into a colder, controlling visual language. Express this quietly through mass, proportion and a few adapted decorative motifs. The native radiating fan relief may be compressed within a broad closed border or terminate beneath a calm horizontal band; wing rays can converge toward their solid roots. Keep this as refined geometric artwork at native scale. The implication should be noticed on a second look. No literal historical Confederate flag, insignia, slogans, shackles, chains, human figures, skulls, devil styling, barbed ornament or giant symbolic emblems. This is spacecraft design with subtle narrative, not a political poster. Preserve the native worn red/ochre surfaces, dark recesses and restrained pale relief. Do not solve the theme with a new black-and-gold paint job.

Keep the main body and collar solid and coherent; no gratuitous decorative cutout. The recessed working cargo bay of L52 remains unchanged and available, with its two longitudinal doors: do NOT fill it, reinterpret it as an unnecessary hole, cover it with a fin, or move its hatch onto the top of the side masses. New aft structure begins BEHIND the moving hatch and does not bridge over it. No hollow skeleton, pipes or loose floating plates. Main silhouette stays within the family demonstrated by native LI and Order; no capital-ship scale or cathedral tower. Spend shape changes on the new wings and aft assembly, not on busy surface detail.

PRESENTATION: a polished, clear production concept sheet on pale grey, original-game-inspired materials with deliberate planar shading. One LARGE side-biased front three-quarter view, nose LEFT, moderately long lens to avoid oversized cabin, showing the new wing planform and stern profile. Supporting FRONT, SIDE, TOP and STOWED views of the SAME ship. Main hull geometry, cockpit, engine count and wing architecture consistent across every view. Stowed view follows the stated mechanism; never shrink the actual panels. Preserve generous proportions and readable depth. No cargo-open inset in this study because its design is unchanged. Labels only concept ID and FRONT / SIDE / TOP / STOWED.

The outer ends turn slightly downward/inward like a compact enclosing cornice; no horn tips, no decorative central notch. WINGS: TWO broad, solid overlapping trapezoidal LEAVES on each side. Together they create a nearly continuous clipped-delta/trapezoid outline, between the native fan and the broad Order wing, with a long straight leading edge, clearly clipped outer tips and a stepped trailing contour. Make them substantial aircraft-like plates of varying width, not the old three thin triangular fan fingers minus one. Keep native red radial artwork, but compress the ray composition toward the roots, with calmer outer panels. Fifth reference: use ONLY the native rotary nesting principle and front root location; reduce to two newly designed full leaves per side. In STOWED rotate these two full-size leaves backward to overlap along the outer hull. New mechanism is proposed, not already validated. Keep L52 hull and cockpit unchanged. The gesture is a compact enclosing stern crown and a broad restrained rotating fan. Label L57.

observations: L52-style paired raised side volumes, recessed central cargo field and Liberty red/ochre panel language remain recognizable.
Aft crosspiece is materially deeper and heavier, with inward-closing ends and a restrained fan relief under its border; this is the principal accepted prompt response, not user approval.
Broad clipped wing outline differs from the previous narrow native fan, but the intended two overlapping leaves are not clearly separated in every view.
STOWED is an illustrative folded silhouette, not proof of rotary hinge clearance or consistent leaf shapes.

Hero perspective exaggerates cockpit size. The native cabin reference DOES contain stepped collar flanges; SIDE/TOP soften and round those source flanges, so their exact contours must come from the native CMP, not the raster. Glazing is broadly recognizable but not proven identical.
Two vertical aft engine apertures are suggested in the side view; no third Order engine is requested.
SIDE and TOP contain perspective, so these are concept supporting views rather than measured orthographic drawings.
modeling_constraints: Reuse native LI cockpit geometry unchanged.
Keep L52 main hull/cargo layout as the iteration base.
Validate two-leaf rotation, aft crown/cargo sweep clearance and actual hardpoint ownership separately before modeling.

variants.mechanism: Proposed Order-style two active prismatic stages per side plus root fairing; independent of L57 rotary proposal.
variants.direction:
L58. AFT: reimagine the spoiler as a SINGLE compact raked trapezoidal DORSAL CREST behind the cargo hatch, rooted on a short solid transverse stern plinth. Borrow the direction of Order's rising aft blade, but make this crest lower and broader through its base, clearly within Order's maximum silhouette and still balanced with the unchanged L52 body. Its leading edge rises diagonally, its top is a blunt sloping facet, and the rear edge is one clean strong step. No extra third engine and no tall narrow spike. A shallow narrow fluted field climbs the crest and ends beneath a heavy plain cap; a small source-like fan motif is visually contained at its base. Preserve source-style metal and paint. This gives a stern standard-like shape through geometry, without a flag or literal emblem.
WINGS: one broad clipped swept plane on each side, composed of TWO ACTIVE NESTED SLIDING SECTIONS and a small fixed root fairing. Follow the coherent Order planform: broad root, long straight diagonal leading edge, flat clipped outer tip, nearly continuous trailing edge. Panels overlap with two purposeful straight joint lines. No spread fan teeth. Fifth reference is the actual Order telescopic wing motion: the two moving stages slide diagonally INWARD into one another and their root, reducing span; they do NOT rotate backward like Liberty fan leaves. STOWED must show the same wing angle and panel shapes nested closer to the hull, not a rotated fan and not shrunken plates. This is a proposed adaptation, not claimed native LI mechanics. Ornament remains restrained and native-Liberty-derived, with inward-directed rays on the inner wing field and calm outer planes. Keep L52 body, its working cargo recess and exact native LI cockpit. Label L58.

Broad clipped continuous wings and bounded linear ornament give a distinct Order-influenced silhouette while keeping LI palette, fan relief and two vertically stacked aft engine faces.
The crest is the bolder of these proposals and needs user review for Liberty character and acceptable height.
STOWED retains wing orientation with reduced span, suggesting telescopic nesting. It does not demonstrate two mechanically complete slider stages or exact nesting depths.

Native collar flanges are rounded into ring-like contours in supporting views; glazing proportions also vary with the view. Reuse native cabin geometry unchanged rather than reconstructing it from this sheet.
SIDE and TOP are not measured orthographic projections; engine positions in TOP are perspectivally displaced.
modeling_constraints: Reuse native LI cockpit geometry unchanged.
Keep L52 main hull/cargo as iteration base and two vertical engines.
